headline: Backup Report for Travis County Homes
summary: Homes in Travis County face an elevated risk. A long outage of 12 hours or more happens about once every 10 years (fact: outlook.once_every_years). This comes from 8 years of records since 2018 (fact: outlook.years_of_data, outlook.since). In February 2021, 43% of homes in the county lost power. The longest-waiting tenth went without power for about 96 hours (fact: event.1.start, event.1.peak_out_pct, event.1.p90_hours). In February 2023, 29% of homes in the county lost power. The longest-waiting tenth went without power for about 132 hours (fact: event.2.start, event.2.peak_out_pct, event.2.p90_hours). One Core lasts about 14 hours in August and about 30 hours in February (fact: backup.short_month, backup.long_month). Two Cores last about 21 hours in August (fact: backup.short_month_two_cores). The suggested number of Cores is 2. Two Cores cover 74% of past 12-hour-plus outage hours (fact: sizing.cores, sizing.share, threshold.hours). Base confirms sizing at install.
